title: October 13 holds the overnight rate around 0.25 percent
summary: The rate decision retained an average unsecured overnight call rate around one quarter of a percent for the intermeeting period. The Policy Board reached that decision by majority. Its operating sentence neither revises the rate nor states a forecast for the next decision. Keeping the numerical guideline steady provides a benchmark against which any same-day changes in term rates or collateral-sensitive prices can be examined.

The meeting concluded at 3:32 p.m. The Bank listed October 16 for the release of its economic assessment and November 22 for the minutes. Information released under other titles on the same day requires its own source and timestamp.

questions.question: Can a change in rate expectations be disentangled from other October 13 news?
questions.detail: Collect timestamps of the rate decision and each accompanying release. Use a common event window if releases coincide, and avoid assigning its full price change to the unchanged overnight setting.

questions.question: How should the target be compared with market data?
questions.detail: Use unsecured overnight transaction rates and an averaging interval consistent with the directive. Secured rates or an individual peak trade do not directly measure performance against it.

questions.question: Did the following report alter the forward path?
questions.detail: Compare the term curve around October 16 with the curve immediately after the meeting. Record macroeconomic data releases in both windows before attributing a movement to the Bank.
